name: Temporal durable multi-step agents
short_definition: Use Temporal for durable multi-step AI agents and long-running business processes: Workflows orchestrate deterministically; Activities run LLM calls, tools, and I/O with retries/timeouts. FastAPI starts/signals/queries workflows; workers run separately. Survives crashes, deploys, and human waits — not a replacement for simple Taskiq/Celery fire-and-forget jobs. As of 2026-07-13: temporalio 1.30.0; official Python tutorials pair Temporal + LiteLLM + FastAPI for agents.
scope_in: When to graduate from queues to Temporal
Workflow vs Activity boundaries for agents (LLM/tool = Activity)
Signals/queries for chat turns; Continue-As-New for long histories
Determinism rules and payload size discipline
Relation to LangGraph/pydantic-ai/OpenAI Agents SDK integrations
scope_out: Full Temporal Cloud ops billing comparison
Non-Python Temporal SDKs beyond boundary notes

defaults.orchestrator: Temporal Workflows for multi-step agents, sagas, human-in-the-loop waits
defaults.side_effects: All LLM, HTTP, DB writes, MCP tool calls inside Activities
defaults.api: FastAPI: start workflow, signal user messages, query state; return workflow_id
defaults.worker: Separate process: temporalio worker on task queue; scale independently
defaults.timeouts: start_to_close on each Activity; schedule_to_close budgets; workflow run timeout as policy
defaults.retries: Activity RetryPolicy with non-retryable error types for business failures
defaults.history: Continue-As-New when event history grows (LLM transcripts are large)
defaults.payloads: Pass ids and summaries; store large blobs in object storage/DB, not history
defaults.local_dev: Temporal CLI dev server; uv add temporalio fastapi litellm uvicorn

use_temporal_when: Multi-step agent must resume after crash/deploy
Need visibility into each step with automatic retries
use_queue_instead_when: Single durable function with retries (email, webhook) — Taskiq/Celery
In-request parallel I/O only — anyio task groups
use_langgraph_inproc_when: Short graph, process can die without resume requirement
Prototype agent logic before promoting steps to Activities
do_not: Don't put non-deterministic LLM calls directly in Workflow code
Don't use Temporal as a dumb job queue for one-liners
Don't store full multi-MB LLM logs in workflow history

do: Keep Workflows deterministic (no random, now, or network in Workflow)
Model each tool/LLM call as Activity with timeouts
Version workflows when changing step order
Use signals for user chat turns; queries for UI state
Idempotent Activities where at-least-once delivery applies
dont: Don't share request-scoped SQLAlchemy session into Activities
Don't infinite-loop agent without max steps / continue-as-new plan
Don't block Workflow thread on long sync CPU
Don't pass unserializable objects (open connections) as args

failure_modes: Non-determinism in Workflow → replay failures after deploy
Event history bloat from large LLM outputs → need Continue-As-New
Activity without timeout hangs worker slot
Missing idempotency → double charge / double email on retry
API and worker code skew (different versions registered)
Using Temporal for single short email → ops complexity tax
Signal lost because workflow already completed
Sandbox import errors when Workflow pulls forbidden modules
anti_patterns: LLM completion inside Workflow deterministic code
One mega-Activity that runs the entire agent (loses step-level durability)
Temporal for every background job including logs
Storing files/base64 blobs in activity results unbounded
No worker process — only API (nothing executes)
Catch-all retry on business validation errors

versions_as_of.note: Tutorial stacks often pin temporalio>=1.12; always lock current SDK in uv.lock

deprecation_watch: DIY durable state machines in Redis without replay semantics for long agents
LangGraph-only persistence when crash-resume across deploys is required (unless external checkpointer is solid)
Sleeping in API processes for human waits
Celery chords as a substitute for long human-in-the-loop sagas without clear need
ts_boundary: Next UI talks to FastAPI; FastAPI talks to Temporal (start/signal/query). Do not run Temporal workers in Vercel serverless. Optional: Temporal TypeScript workers for TS-only activities — prefer one language for agent activities unless polyglot is intentional. UI polls query or subscribes via SSE from API that queries workflow.
rust_boundary: CPU-heavy activities can be separate workers in Rust on same task queue if payloads are JSON-compatible; orchestration stays Temporal. Rare for LLM agents — Python activities dominate.
supabase_boundary: Persist conversation snapshots and business entities in Postgres; workflow history is not your product DB. Activities use service credentials with idempotent upserts. Store workflow_id on the conversation row for resume. Human approval flags can be written by Activity after signal.
boundary_contracts: workflow_id / run_id returned from OpenAPI start endpoint
MCP tools invoked only inside Activities when used

decision_matrix_row.problem_class: Durable multi-step agent / long business process
decision_matrix_row.python: Temporal Workflow + Activities; FastAPI control plane
decision_matrix_row.ts: UI + optional TS activities; start via Python API preferred

threats: Malicious signal payloads causing unsafe Activity args
PII retained indefinitely in event history
Tool injection via LLM plans executed without policy checks
mitigations: Auth on start/signal/query HTTP APIs; authorize workflow ownership
Least-privilege worker secrets; separate task queues for risky tools
Validate signal payloads with Pydantic in Workflow/Activity boundary
Continue-As-New + external store to limit PII in history; retention policies
Allowlist tools the agent may run; human confirm high-risk Activities

must_generate: Workflow/Activity split with LLM and tools in Activities
must_not_generate: Unbounded history growth without Continue-As-New strategy
Worker embedded only in-process in uvicorn without clear prod plan
Passing SQLAlchemy Session into Activity args

tests_required: Activity unit tests with mocked LLM/tools
ci_gates: Ban network imports in workflow modules via lint/arch test if possible

negative: Temporal used only for send_email single activity without multi-step need
Huge transcript strings stored every step without CAN

skill_module_bullets: Temporal for durable multi-step agents/sagas — not simple mailer queues
Workflow deterministic; LLM/tools/IO in Activities with timeouts/retries
Continue-As-New for long chat histories; store blobs outside history
Signals for user turns; queries for UI state
temporalio 1.30.0 as_of 2026-07-13; pair with LiteLLM in Activities

checklist: Problem needs durability beyond a queue job
conflicts_noted: LangGraph vs Temporal: graphs for in-process control flow; Temporal for durable execution — can combine but don't double-orchestrate blindly

Single large Activity wrapping whole agent is simpler but sacrifices step durability — default recommend fine-grained Activities for tools
